text: Gerugu (Japanese: , Gurerī) is a Nopon in Xenoblade Chronicles . He is a Nopon Merchant, and can be found at the Traveller's Rest on the Bionis' Leg. He is Tuzu's husband and Pachipa's father, and travels with Batubatu. He is very knowledgeable about the Mythical Empress.

Getting Bigger! (Japanese: , Okkiku Na~re) is a quest in . It can be received from Dabidabi near the Chief's Residence, on a balcony west of the Mysterious Sanctuary of Frontier Village. Riki must be in the lead. In the course of the quest's objectives, the quest Who is Bigger? will be triggered and must be first completed. After Getting Bigger! is completed, Riki's Cowardice skill branch will be unlocked.

The Gem Man's Stall (Japanese: , Jemu-jii no Rotenshō) is a landmark in . It is located in the Commercial District of Colony 9, just north of the Ether Light. The Gem Man is found here. Next to him is a Gem Crafting Machine. For the first part of the game, this is the only place gems can be crafted. The Spanner can be found around here. Later on, a quest can be received from him, in which an Ultra Small Reactor must be obtained. It can only be found by upgrading all the levels to level 1 in the reconstruction of Colony 6. Once he is given the reactor, he will give the party the Mobile Furnace, which allows gems to be crafted at any time. In , a Time Attack portal can be found next to it.

The General's Boots are light feet armour in . They are Dunban's initial feet armour when he rejoins the party at Colony 6. The description implies that Dunban was a general in the Colony 9 Defence Force before the Monado crippled his right arm at the Battle of Sword Valley. General's Boots are not otherwise obtainable.

The General's Belt is light legs armour in . It is Dunban's initial legs armour when he joins the party at Colony 6. Its description implies that Dunban was a general in the Colony 9 Defence Force before the use of the Monado crippled his right arm. The General's Belt is not otherwise obtainable.

General's Gauntlets are light arms armour in . They are Dunban's initial arms armour when he joins the party at Colony 6 and are otherwise unavailable. Their description implies that Dunban was a general in the Colony 9 Defence Force before the Monado crippled his arm at the Battle of Sword Valley.

Gaur Plain (Japanese: , Gauru Heigen) is a location in . It is located on the lower level of Bionis' Leg, and describes the whole area between Jabos Rock Rest Area and Viliera Hill. The music track for the Bionis' Leg area is named "Gaur Plain" as well. This is the biggest free-roaming location on Bionis' Leg.

The General's Attire is light torso armour in . It is Dunban's initial torso equipment, implying that Dunban was a general in the Colony 9 Defence Force before his use of the Monado crippled his right arm. General's Attire is not otherwise available.
Gemini Gear (Japanese: , Jemini Gia) is medium head armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are helmets that appear to be made of Homs technology, taken by Mechon.
Gemini Armour is medium torso armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is made from Homs technology that was taken by Mechon.
Frozen Gauntlets are medium arms armour in Xenoblade Chronicles.
Gemini Leggings are medium legs armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They were made from Homs technology that was taken by the Mechon during the first war between Bionis and Mechonis.
Gemini Boots are medium feet armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are made from Homs technology taken by the Mechon.
Gemini Gauntlets are medium arms armour in Xenoblade Chronicles.

Gentle Mother Armu (Japanese: , Onkōna Bikkumamu) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Armu family. It can be found at level 37 near the Agora Shore in eastern Colony 9, accompanied by some level 31 - 35 Baby Armu. It has been known to run towards the water when low on health; should it successfully reach the water, it will exit the battle, resetting its position and regaining full health. It can drop the Maternal Armu Milk needed for Thawing Relations.
The Gale Shot (Japanese: , Geirushotto) is a weapon in . It is an ether rifle wielded by Sharla, and can be dropped by various low- to mid-level enemies. Gale Shots are also available for trade.

Gentle Rodriguez (Japanese: , Jūnanna Rodorigesu, lit. Flexible Rodriguez) is a Unique Monster in . It is a member of the Brog family, and is found at level 40. It can be found in the far north end of Agora Shore in Colony 9. It is backed into a cave, guarding the Message in a Bottle quest Key Item needed for Liliana's Sincere Request. However, it is possible to get the item by luring it out then running and sneaking behind its back. It can drop the Laughing Brog Bags needed for Désirée's Apology.

Gadolt's Rifle (Japanese: , Gadokasutamuraifuru, Gadolt Custom Rifle) is a weapon in . It is an ether rifle, usable by Sharla. It is given by Otharon after defeating Xord in the Ether Mine's Central Pit. This rifle used to be Gadolt's weapon of choice. After Mechon invaded Colony 6, Galdolt and Otharon planned a surprise attack to free the captured Homs. The attack was unsuccessful, and Gadolt went missing. Otharon found his rifle afterwards.
General Drivers (Japanese: , Jenerarubankā) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are gunlances wielded by Reyn.

Generic Shafts are rare materials in . They can be obtained from Mechon M64 on Bionis' Leg or Mechon M64X in the Ether Mine. Generic Shafts are also available via trade with three NPCs. According to their description, they are quality parts of great versatility and they can be used in any kind of machine. Generic Blades, Generic Cranks, Generic Plugs, and Generic Units share this description. Two Generic Shafts are required for Materials for a Mixer.

Generic Blades are rare materials in . They can be obtained from Mechon on Bionis' Leg and the Ether Mine, or traded for with Ma'crish after she moves to Colony 6. According to their description, they are quality parts of great versatility and they can be used in any kind of machine. Generic Shafts, Generic Cranks, Generic Plugs, and Generic Units share this description. Two Generic Blades are needed for Materials for a Mixer.

Furious Jozan (Japanese: , Fundo no Jōzan) is a Unique Monster in . It is a Licorne-type member of the Telethia family, and can be found at level 96 at the Telethia Laboratory in the High Entia Tomb. A High Entia Emblem is required to reach this area, so the following quests must be completed before it can be reached: # The Imperial Ceremony # Imperial Ceremony Offerings

Frost Nebulae (Japanese: , Furosuto Nebura) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Nebula family, and can be found at level 80 in the Satorl Marsh, near the Sororal Statues or Kelsher Wetland during fog, replacing Aqua Nebulae. They are one of only two enemies to drop Level V Chill Plus crystals. They are the only source of Glacier Elements, which are needed to complete the quest Replica Monado 3.
General Arachnos (Japanese: , Jeneraru Supaido) are enemies in . They are members of the Arachno family, and can be found at level 73-74 in Windy Cave on the Bionis' Leg.
This page is a list of all the Unique Monsters in Galahad Fortress.

Gem Man (Japanese: , Jemu-jii) is a Homs in . He is the owner of the Gem Man's Stall and he is found any time at this landmark. The Gem Man operates an Ether Furnace, which is capable of processing Ether Crystals and Ether Cylinders into gems. The Gem Man does not charge the party for using his Furnace. Initially the party must visit the Gem Man any time they want to craft a gem. After completing The Gem Man's Invention, the Gem Man gives them a Mobile Furnace, which allows the party to craft gems anywhere. In , it is revealed that the Gem Man's ether furnace is still standing in Colony 9, albeit unusably damaged. After completing The Derelict Ether Furnace, Nikol fixes the ether furnace, al

Getting to Know Minnie (Japanese: , Meinī wo Shiru) is a quest in . It can be received from Minnie on the bridge at southwest of the Residential District of Colony 9. If Shulk is in the active party, he will comment.

Getting to Know Dorothy (Japanese: , Dorotea wo Shiru) is a quest in . It can be received from Dorothy near the main entrance to the Commercial District of Colony 9. If Melia is in the active party, she will comment.

Get the 3rd Lift Moving (Japanese: , Dai-3 Rifuto wo Kidōshiro) is a Story Quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is received automatically once the party reaches the 2nd Lift - 1F while progressing through Mechonis Field.

Ged Fortress (Japanese: , Geto Toride) is a landmark in . It is the first of the Mechon facilities encountered in Sword Valley. It bears resemblance to a pyramid and is devoid of enemies. It houses the control device that unlocks the device for the 6th Gate. There are no Surprise Quests here, unlike the other two facilities.
This page is a list of all the Unique Monsters in Frontier Village.
Genuine Plugs (Japanese: , Junsei puragu buhin) are rare materials in . They can be obtained from Mechon M31 during the attack on Colony 9. Genuine Plugs are also available via trade.

Generic Plugs are rare materials in . They can be obtained from M32 Scout Units and Mechon M32 on Bionis' Leg, and Mechon M32X in the Ether Mine. Generic Plugs are also available via trade. According to their description, they are quality parts of great versatility and they can be used in any kind of machine. Generic Blades, Generic Cranks, Generic Shafts, and Generic Units share this description.

Generic Units are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can only be obtained via trade with Elior and Talonyth. According to their description, they are quality parts of great versatility and they can be used in any kind of machine. Generic Blades, Generic Cranks, Generic Plugs, and Generic Shafts share this description.

Generic Cranks are rare materials in . They can be obtained from M42 Scout Units on Bionis' Leg and in the Ether Mine. Generic Cranks are also available via trade. According to their description, they are quality parts of great versatility and they can be used in any kind of machine. Generic Blades, Generic Shafts, Generic Plugs, and Generic Units share this description.

Geography Lesson (Japanese: , Kyoshinkai no Arukikata, Walking on the Bionis) is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located at the Believer's Paradise on the Bionis' Leg, between Dunban and Shulk at purple affinity.
Gerugu's Letter is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is Gerugu's reply to Daza's Letter for Secret Mission. Gerugu gives it to the party to deliver to Daza.

Full Metal Jaguar (Japanese: ) is a Class featured in . This class provides bonuses to melee accuracy, ranged accuracy, and evasion. It is one of six final classes and can only be leveled up from Winged Viper. The playable characters of this class include Elma. Full Metal Jaguar has four Skill slots. Neilnail's class is an Alternative Full Metal Jaguar.

Gatling Guns are ranged weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are the ranged weapons for Shield Trooper and Bastion Warrior Classes. Gatling guns are also the ranged weapons used by Lin, Frye, and Nagi.

Gather Information (Japanese: , Jōhō wo Ero) is a Surprise Quest in . It is automatically triggered in Satorl Marsh during the course of Adviser Hunt, received from Gadada in Frontier Village. In , it is listed as a Timed Quest and expires after the events at the Mechonis Core.

Gadolt's Gun Turret is a rare material in Xenoblade Chronicles. For unknown reasons, it was cut from the game. It was most likely intended to be dropped by Gadolt after he is fought as Jade Face in Mechonis Field.

Futures That Lie Ahead (それぞれの未来へ, To One's Own Future) is an Event Track in Xenoblade Chronicles, composed and arranged by Manami Kiyota. It is track 18 of disc 1 from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack. This music is a heartwarming theme that is heard during the cutscene when Melia addresses her subjects in Alcamoth as the new crown princess after her trial in the High Entia Tomb, and later at the end of the game as Fiora wanders Colony 9 in the new world created by Shulk and the others after Zanza's demise.

The Ganglion Antropolis (Japanese: , Gurousu Dōkutsu Kichi, Growth Cave Base) is an Unexplored Territory in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Ganglion base located in caverns directly beneath Cauldros's G'nahan Villa, and can only be accessed by crossing the lava field northeast of FN Site 505. It must be entered on foot, as the entrance is too small for Skells. As with all Unexplored Territories, its discovery yields an achievement (Invading the Ganglion Antropolis). The entrance to the Antropolis is blocked by a transparent barrier which cannot be removed until a key is obtained during Definian Downfall, and similar barriers block access to parts of the Antropolis until three more keys are o

Ga Jiarg (Japanese: , Ga Derugu, Ga Derg; English dub: or ), or Prince Jiarg to his subjects, is a character in . He is a Wrothian first seen speaking to Luxaar along with his companion Ga Buidhe. He then is seen retrieving a Ganglion mech from New Los Angeles. He is a former prince who is only helping the Ganglion to prevent his people from being used as cannon fodder.

Gadolt's Cannon were weapons designed for Xenoblade Chronicles. They were rifles to be wielded by Sharla, however for unknown reasons, they were cut from the final game. It was most likely intended to be dropped by Gadolt after he is fought as Jade Face in Mechonis Field along with Gadolt's Gun Turret.

no7=G-LOW-S→F.S.K.O is a track in Xenoblade Chronicles X composed and arranged by Hiroyuki Sawano. It is track seven of disc one from the XenobladeX Original Soundtrack, and the seventh part of the suite titled 0rCH-SUITE "X". The first half of this track is heard in the following cutscenes: * Meeting Goetia for the first time in Chapter 4 * The appearance of the Wrothians in Chapter 9 * Luxaar resolving to infiltrate the Lifehold Core himself in Chapter 12 The second half of this track is heard in the following cutscenes: * After defeating Goetia in Chapter 4. The music continues after she is rescued by an alien Skell. * Cross's arm being blown off in Chapter 5 * Lin attempting to fix a Ske

The Ganglion (Japanese: , Gurousu, Growth; English dub: or ) is a hostile coalition of different alien races in . The alliance is a crime syndicate composed of various races originating from the Samaar Federation, founded and headed by the Ganglion, a creation of the rouge Samaarian scientist Void, whose mind had deteriorated during the eons spent imprisoned in the Rift Between Worlds. Under the command of Void, the Ganglion were trying to wipe out from existence the descendant races of the Samaarians, which included Elma's race and the human race, believing to be their destiny to do so, as Void had encoded a genetic failsafe in the Ganglions' DNA; thusly, the Ganglion were certain that the

Gerhardt, the Lone and Proud (Japanese: , Kokō no Gēaharuto) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Mephite family. It can be found at level 12 in Noctilum in the largest room in the Whale's Nostril. It is accompanied by several Mischievous Mephites, and does not spawn until the field treasure is approached.

The Garden Spring (Japanese: , Teien Yūsui) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a small body of water located in Noctilum, north of Sapphire Table and south of the Humdrum Peaks. The FN Site 221 is here, as is one entrance to the Ensanguined Font.
Gardener Mortifoles (Japanese: , Gāden Foriumu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Mortifoles and can be found at level 22-23 or at level 27-28 in the Canopied Nightwood in Noctilum.
Fukai Pass (Japanese: , Fukai Yamamichi) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in the highlands of Noctilum, north of Qing Long Glade.
Gate Puges (Japanese: , Gēto Berude) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Puge machines, Ganglion's human size robots, and can be found at level 7-8 on the Far Isle of Tzu'o in Cauldros.

Garnet Forfexes (Japanese: , Gānetto Pagurusu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Forfex family, and can be found at level 16-19 by the lake south of Tripod Rock in Noctilum.
Garnet Saltats (Japanese: , Gānetto Sarutāto) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Saltat family, and can be found at level 51-53 on Fallshorn Isle in Primordia.

Ghillie Falsaxums (Japanese: , Girī Garukasu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Falsaxum family, and can be found at level 31-33 at Middle Hushflood or at level 40 in the Vitriol Cesspool in Noctilum.

Galdr (Japanese: , Garudora) are a type of Ganglion Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can transform between a humanoid state and a bird-like cruise state. Galdr can be found inactive in cruise mode, but some are just dormant and will attack if approached. They can be found in all five regions, but are most common in Ganglion-controlled regions like Sylvalum and Cauldros.
Gehenna Lophids (Japanese: , Gehena Rofiru) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Lophid family, and can be found at level 56-57 near FN Site 506 in Cauldros.
Germivores (Japanese: , Burōsu) are small insectoids in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They often mimic flowers, though their legs can give them away. They can be found in all five regions.
Ghost Adseculas (Japanese: , Gōsuto Apisu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Adsecula family, and can be found at level 51-54 at East Ibra Ravine in Oblivia.
Garnet Scirpos (Japanese: , Gānetto Shirunea) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Scirpo family, and can be found at level 51-52 in Noctilum's Weeping Whitewood.
Ghost Factory is one of Elma's two Signature Arts in . It allows allies to avoid a fixed number of enemy attacks. Cross can learn it by completing Then and Now.

Gerome is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He can be found at West Melville Street during the day and near North Founders Street at night in the Commercial District of New Los Angeles. He is a member of the Reclaimers Division.
Fullbelly Geckos (Japanese: , Manpukuyamori) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Oblivia. Three are needed for Bread and a Circus.

Garudo Pellionia Minimas (Japanese: , Garudosanshousou) are prime collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be rarely found in Primordia's caves such as the Beasts' Lair. Five are needed for the Basic Mission Ovah Overdrive.
Gesture Gloves (Japanese: , Jesuchatinā) are rare collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Noctilum. Six of them are needed for the mission Reclaiming the Whale.

Galjim Crystals (Japanese: , Garujīmu no Suishō) are unique collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Noctilum, in particular through the Weeping Whitewood. Eight of them are required for Research on a Budget.
Fullerene Corals (Japanese: , Furaren no Sango) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Sylvalum.

Gadolinium Petramands (Japanese: , Gadoriniumu Aranea) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Petramand family and can be found at level 43-45 near FN Site 508 at Sunset Falls, at FN Site 504 inside the canyon leading to Wildcat Fortress, or at Kw'arah Cloister in Cauldros.

Gehenna Span (Japanese: , Meifu no Hashi, Bridge of Hell) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a natural bridge located in Sylvalum. It serves as a direct passage between Delusians North Summit and Delusians South Summit, over Hardheart Canyon. There are no enemies on the span itself, but a group of Prankster Mephites and Lask, the Unscrupulous reside on a ledge directly below.

The Ganglion Weapons Hangar (Japanese: , Gurousu Heiki Kakunōko) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Cauldros, within the larger O'rrh Sim Castle Ruins. It is an enormous megastructure approximately 800 meters wide, including the immediate outer wall. (By comparison, New Los Angeles is about 1900 meters wide, including its outer wall.) The roof of the hangar is dominated by an approximately 650-meter-wide metal iris that can open and close to accommodate large craft; when closed, the roof resembles a giant metal colosseum. The hangar can technically be visited on foot as soon as the player can explore Cauldros, but both the hangar and much of the path leading to it are fil
Germaine, the Treasure Keeper (Japanese: , Gohō no Jerumēnu) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Ovis family. It can be found at level 35 near Eddie's Conquest in Oblivia.

Froste, the Courteous (, Onkōna Furosuto) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Vesper family. It can be found at level 50 at the tunnel at the far end of the Vitriol Cesspool in Noctilum. Killing it is required for segment recon.

Gesserith, the Wileworm (Japanese: , Rōkainaru Geseritto) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Sabula family. It can be found at level 76 at South Silent Sandsea in Sylvalum after being summoned by Atreides, the Distinguished. Killing it is required for segment recon.
Gadaf, the Pulverizer (Japanese: , Funsai no Gadafu) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Marnuck Ganglion member. It can be found at level 30 inside the North Ant's Nest in Oblivia.

Ga-uhl, the Precept-Keeper (Japanese: , Kairitsu no Ga-uru) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Fal-swo machine. It can be found at level 50 at Badr Stronghold in Sylvalum during nighttime.

The Frontline Medic Quo (Japanese: , Kasenkyūgo-kei Kuō) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Quo machine. It can be found at level 40 at the Ganglion Weapons Hangar in Cauldros. From the O'rrh Sim Gate entrance, the tyrant is found at the eastern wing accompanied by two Marnuck Imperials.

Gadaf's Qmoeva (Japanese: , Gadafu Sen'yō Kumūba) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Qmoeva Ganglion's skell. It can be found at level 31 under a tree in Primordia Waters. It will be hidden until approached. It is the Qmoeva of Gadaf, the Pulverizer.
Gale Auravises (Japanese: , Geiru Akuira) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Auravis family, and can be found at level 27-30 at Oblivia Ingress in Oblivia.
Frozen Pizza is an Important Item in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is needed as a bargaining tool with Aganeba during the course of The Pip-Squeak.

in New Los Angeles]] The Gaur (English dub: ) are a race of beings in . They are Skell-sized living weapons created by the Ganglion. A number of Gaur, including Rock, were used to attack a Qlurian village, killing many people. Rock defected and took Celica with him. Rock is the only Gaur to appear in-game. He is first met along with Celica in Noctilum during Manhunt, and becomes a construction worker in New Los Angeles after New in New LA.

Gaia Gularth (Japanese: , Gaia Gurāsu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Gularth family, and two can be found in Cauldros anytime except during brimstone rain, during which they are replaced by Ymir Gularth. One can be found at level 64 standing by the Titan's Table, while another can be found at level 71 walking through the lava near Dragonbone Promontory.
Galba Vassago (Japanese: , Garuba Vasago) is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He can be found at the Port Side of the Ma-non Ship in New Los Angeles during the day.

Ga Bewhe (Japanese: , Ga Biyu) is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. After completing the mission Gold Rush, she can be found at the upper cliffs of the Cryptic Sign in Oblivia in rainy weather, overlooking the Wrothian Stronghold. When spoken to, she will give Cross 200,000 credits before taking her leave.
The Ghosts (Japanese: , Gōsuto) are aggressive and mostly unknowable entities in .
Gadd (Japanese: , Gaddo) is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He is a Human who can be found at Noctilum's Waterway Tangle or Oblivia's Great Washington Isle.
Gentle Approach is a Skill in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is unlocked as a Psycorruptor at rank 4.
Ge Jewhe (Japanese: , Ge Jiyu) is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She can be found at the Wrothian Stronghold in Oblivia after completing the mission Until the End.

Ganglion Command (Japanese: , Gurousu Kanbu) is a subcategory in Xenoblade Chronicles X. This is the subcategory the commanders of the Ganglion are designated. There are three known commanders and they are all Bosses.

The Gaff Pugilith (Japanese: , Gyafu Berudero) is a Mission Exclusive Enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Pugilith family, and can be found at level 21 at the Seabird's Beak in Sylvalum. Defeating it is required during Bottoms Up.
Frontier Spirit (Japanese: , Furontia Tamashii) is a Normal Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It can be received from Corwin at Division Drive in the Administrative District of New Los Angeles.

The Galdr Raven (Japanese: , Garudora Reivun) is a Mission Exclusive Enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a level 37 Galdr piloted by TP351: Tempera. It is first mentioned during Frontier Spirit as the mysterious black Skell that attacks Bates, and is encountered by the party if route B is chosen, though it is not fought during that mission. It reappears during Unknown Assailant, hunting down the members of Team Corwin, and is fought at the entrance to Sylvalum's Banshee Cave.
Germivores No More is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from the Interceptors and the primary destination is Noctilum.

Gale Qmoevas (Japanese: , Geiru Kumūba) are a pair of Mission Exclusive Enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are level 41–50 Qmoevas, and must be defeated on Sylvalum's Northern Searoad during White Lifehold.
Gaga for Guavas is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from the diner chef and the primary destination is Noctilum to obtain Socha Guavas.
Garlic 2.0 is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from the Integrated Production Plant and the primary destination is Oblivia.
Gathering Grenades is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from the Mediators and the primary destination is Sylvalum.
Gathering Thunder is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from a male Wrothian and the primary destination is Sylvalum.
The G-Piledriver is a superweapon for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is known as Drillpile in the Japanese version.

The Gale Milsaadi (Japanese: , Geiru Mirusādo) is a Mission Exclusive Enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. He is a Milsaadi Ganglion, and is fought at level 52 at Eddie's Conquest in Oblivia during Yelv's Partner.
Garbled Guardians is a Heart-to-Heart in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located at Ishmael Hills in the Residential District of New Los Angeles between Bozé and Cross during the evening.

The Garuda Jacul (Japanese: , Garūdo Hasutara) is a Mission Exclusive Enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a level 39 member of the Jacul family, and is fought an Oblivia's Kintrees during A New Life. Its arts include Roar (physical), Spiral Lance (electrical), Tail Twirl (physical), Thunder Shot (electrical)
Gerrid Shells are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Gerrids, specifically from their back appendages. They are components of Evasion Up and SpecUp.EVA augments.
Gerrid Navels are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Gerrids.
Galdr Heads are rare materials in . They can be obtained from the heads of Galdrs. Twenty-four are required to craft an Overdrive Green Bonus augment. One is required for Skell Repair: Head.
Germivore A is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a green germivore variant. It can be obtained from Lomoth, the Beast-Eater in Oblivia.
Germivore B is a Holofigure in . It depicts a purple germivore variant. It can be obtained from Florence, the Hell Maggot in Sylvalum at night.
Gerrid A is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a red gerrid variant. It can be obtained from Bartley, the Conflagration in Cauldros.
Gerrid B is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a beige gerrid variant. It can be obtained from Daemon, the Undertaker in Sylvalum.
Galdr A is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a black galdr variant wielding the piercing beam weapons. It can be obtained from Armed Recon Galdr in Cauldros.
Galdr B is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a black galdr variant wielding the tornado claw weapons. It can be obtained from Armed Engineer Galdr in Cauldros.
Galdr C is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a black galdr variant wielding the titan missile weapons. It can be obtained from the Air Support Galdr in Cauldros.
Galdr E is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a red galdr variant wielding the piercing beam weapons. It can be obtained from Lyla's Galdr in Sylvalum.
Galdr F is a Holofigure in . It depicts a gold galdr variant wielding the tornado claw weapons. It can be obtained from Chantai's Galdr in Cauldros.
Galdr G is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a blue galdr variant wielding the titan missile weapons. It can be obtained from Duran's Galdr in Noctilum.
Galdr H is a Holofigure in . It depicts a green galdr variant wielding the creed revolver weapons. It can be obtained from Vendura's Galdr in Oblivia.

Fulge Series is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a Grenada Galactic Group Photon Saber. It is obtained as a reward for completing the Vegetables category of the Oblivia Collectopedia. The Fulge weapons available in-game are: * Archetype Fulge * Iron Fulge * Carbide Fulge * Cermet Fulge * Chrome Fulge * Chromoly Fulge * Cobalt Fulge * Titanium Fulge * Ceramic Fulge * Diamond Fulge

If it was triggered by the party leader's use of an Art or Special, or by the third Special of a Blade Combo, the combo's name is displayed in large text across the center of the screen.
